subject.title: [Security] Potential Model-Generated Secret Leak in Anthropic SSE Parse Errors

question: Should OpenClaw treat raw Anthropic SSE payloads in parse exceptions as defense-in-depth hardening to remove now, despite the absence of a demonstrated OpenClaw trust-boundary violation?
rationale: Repository policy does not classify user-controlled credential exposure as a vulnerability without OpenClaw impact, but retaining arbitrary model output in exception text is avoidable and may become hazardous when deployments forward errors to shared logging systems.

options.title: Harden the error path
options.body: Remove raw content, preserve bounded structural diagnostics and a digest, add secret-sentinel regression coverage, and coordinate the canonical provider fix upstream.

options.title: Require boundary proof first
options.body: Keep the behavior unchanged until a private report demonstrates that a shipped OpenClaw path persists the exception where a less-trusted party can access it.

recommendation.title: Harden the error path
recommendation.body: Remove raw content, preserve bounded structural diagnostics and a digest, add secret-sentinel regression coverage, and coordinate the canonical provider fix upstream.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice combines OpenClaw's documented security scope with ownership of dependency integration and release-facing security handling.
